title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers created deepfake videos and fake social media profiles impersonating a real, named immigration attorney to solicit cash payments from immigrants seeking legal help. The failure here is deliberate AI-enabled impersonation, not a malfunction of a deployed product, and it happened at the point where members of the public encounter AI-generated content on consumer social media platforms. The scale was substantial, with thousands of fraudulent accounts across multiple platforms before removal efforts began.

The impersonation succeeded in part because the platforms hosting the content did not catch it before victims were deceived. Detection required the real attorney to notice inbound calls from confused potential clients and then hire a specialist firm to locate and remove the accounts. No automated platform-level check identified the fraudulent profiles at creation or shortly after, and the accounts persisted in large numbers until targeted removal was requested.

It is not established who the scammers are, where they operate from, or whether any law enforcement action has been taken against them. The reported victim losses and account counts come from the attorney and press reporting, not from a law enforcement finding or platform audit.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become a target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using deepfake videos and fake social media profiles to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals have created hundreds of fraudulent accounts across multiple platforms, generating AI-generated images and videos of Leal promoting immigration services he never offered. In one scam, a digital version of Leal falsely offers US residency assistance for $2,200 cash to undocumented immigrants without deportation orders. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and he estimates the fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months.

In response, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake social media profiles, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically direct victims through WhatsApp to request payments via digital transfer services like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scammers. He is warning immigrants to verify the identities of anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of social media ads promising immigration benefits in exchange for immediate payment.
